title: CorrectionObject
description: The atomic unit of transcript intelligence. Represents one proposed change against the immutable canonical Deepgram baseline. Produced by either a deterministic rule or an AI specialty prompt. Reviewed by a human court reporter.

id.description: ULID prefixed with 'corr_'. Immutable once assigned.

case_id.description: The case that owns this transcript. Enforced by RLS.

specialty.description: Which specialty produced this correction. 'deterministic_rule' is used when the source is a rule module rather than an AI prompt.

prompt_version.description: Version of the specialty prompt (or rule module) that produced this correction. For deterministic corrections, the rule's version.

paragraph_id.description: ID of the paragraph in the canonical transcript.

start_word_id.description: First word of the affected range.

end_word_id.description: Last word of the affected range (inclusive).

start_offset_ms.description: Millisecond offset from start of audio.

type.description: Determines which further fields are required. punctuation_edit is a text change (before/after, word tokens must be identical — punctuation/casing only). paragraph_split is structural. See per-type constraints in the audit document.

before.description: Text as it appears in the canonical. Required for text-substitution types; absent for structural types.

after.description: Proposed text. Required for text-substitution types.

reason.description: Human-readable explanation. Displayed to the reporter in the CorrectionsPanel. Empty or generic reasons ('improved clarity', 'looks better') are rejected by the validator.

reason_kind.description: Category of reasoning. Used for filtering and metrics.

confidence.description: 0.0 = no confidence; 1.0 = maximum. Corrections below 0.5 are rendered as low-confidence in the UI and require explicit accept.

confidence_source.description: Explanation of how confidence was derived. E.g., 'registry+deepgram_low_confidence' or 'phonetic_edit_distance_1'.

provider.description: AI provider name for source=='ai'. E.g., 'anthropic', 'openai', 'google', 'local'.

model.description: Actual model ID used. E.g., 'claude-opus-4-7'. Version-locked.

prompt_versions.description: Map of prompt component name to version used. E.g., {'system_role': 'v1', 'specialty/proper_name_novel': 'v3'}. Enables exact replay.

context_hash.description: Hash of the exact context envelope submitted with this call. Enables exact replay.

supporting_evidence.description: Optional evidence pointers that back up the correction. Rendered as tooltips in the UI.

state.description: Current lifecycle state. Transitions logged in correction_decisions.

decided_by.description: User ID of the reporter who made the decision. Null while pending.

decision_note.description: Optional free-text note from the reporter. Especially useful for reject and edit decisions.

final_value.description: For state='edited', the reporter's modified version of change.after (or structural_change).

applied_to_working_transcript.description: True after the correction has been merged into the working transcript projection.

reverted_at.description: Non-null if the correction was later reverted.

pending_reason.description: Set when review.state is accepted/edited but applied_to_working_transcript is false: the correction is accepted, its apply is deferred. E.g. 'structural_apply_engine_v2' for qa_split and other structural changes whose canonical restructuring is not yet implemented. The workspace shows 'accepted — apply pending' rather than treating it as a silent no-op.

example_proper_name_correction.reason: Case registry entry 'Baer Imaging' matches phonetically; Deepgram confidence on 'Bayer' was 0.62.

example_qa_split.reason: Paragraph contains an inline question followed by an answer; text after 'You understand that?' is a witness affirmation.
